name: Prithu
role: First consecrated king, remembered as an avatar of Vishnu
summary: Prithu is described in the Mahabharata and Puranas as the first consecrated king. The earth, Prithvi, is named for him, and he is said to have milked her to bring grain and plants for everyone.
about: Many Puranas and the Mahabharata describe Prithu as a chakravartin, a universal king, and the first to be consecrated as ruler of the earth. Hindu tradition regards him as an avatar of Vishnu. In the Vishnu Purana, his father Vena neglected the Vedic rituals, the sages ended his rule, and the land fell into famine and had no heir. The sages then churned Vena's body, and Prithu came from the right arm. The Bhagavata Purana adds that Archi, his future wife, came with him. The earth was bare and fled him in the form of a cow, but agreed to give her gifts if he protected her. He milked her with the help of Manu as the calf, which led to farming, villages and trade. Because of this, the earth is called Prithvi, daughter of Prithu. The Mahabharata and the Puranas also describe a golden age during his reign. The Bhagavata Purana says he performed ninety-nine horse sacrifices, and later retired to the forest.
kidSummary: Prithu was the first king crowned to rule the whole earth, say the Puranas. When the earth hid her treasures, he milked her like a cow so everyone could have grain and plants. That is why the earth is called Prithvi, 'Prithu's daughter'. He also levelled rough land to make fields and villages.

story.title: A kingdom without a king
story.text: Prithu's father, King Vena, ignored the rituals, and the sages ended his rule. Without a ruler there was famine, so the sages churned Vena's body, and Prithu came out of his arm.

story.title: The earth hides her gifts
story.text: The hungry people asked Prithu for help. But the earth had stopped giving, and she ran away from him in the form of a cow.

story.title: A promise
story.text: When he chased her, the cow-earth stopped and asked him to treat her well. She promised to give everything living beings needed if he would protect her.

story.title: Milking the earth
story.text: Prithu chose Manu as the calf and milked her. Grain, plants and fruits came, and then the sages, the gods and many others took their own gifts.

story.title: Fields and villages
story.text: He levelled rough ground and set up villages, so people could farm and trade. From then on the earth was called Prithvi, 'the daughter of Prithu'.

teaches: A good ruler cares for the earth and everyone on it
Everyone should get what they need
Respect for the land that feeds us
emblems: Wheel-shaped mark on the right hand (Vishnu Purana)
Lotus mark on the feet (Bhagavata Purana)

facts.text: The Vayu Purana says Prithu stood at birth with bow, arrows and armour, and calls him Adiraja, the first king. The Shatapatha Brahmana calls him the first anointed king.
In the Vishnu Purana, after Vena's rule ended in famine, the sages churned his body, first the thigh and then the right arm. From the right arm Prithu emerged.
In the Vishnu Purana the sages first churned Vena's thigh, and a dark dwarf hunter named Nishada came out, said to carry Vena's evil. Only then did Prithu rise from the right arm.
In the Vishnu Purana the heavens gave Prithu a celestial bow called Ajagava and arrows. The Bhagavata Purana adds a throne, crown, sceptre, sword, shield, horses and cows from various deities.
Prithu's birth was treated as a sacrifice by Brahma, and from it came the first royal bards, the Sutas and Magadhas, who sang the new king's glories.
In the Mahabharata, Vishnu crowned Prithu and entered his body, so that everyone would bow to the king as they bow to Vishnu himself.
The Manu Smriti treats Prithvi as Prithu's wife, not his daughter, so in that text the earth takes her name from her husband.
Scholar Oldham suggests the word chakravarti may come from Prithu's birthmark, the discus sign, rather than from ruling the world. Its literal meaning is 'in whom the wheel abides'.
In the Mahabharata's list of milkings, Meru, prince of mountains, was the milker for the mountains, the Eastern hill was the calf, gems and herbs were the milk, and stones the vessels.
In the Mahabharata, many beings each milked the earth in their own way. Trees took buds, the sages took the Vedas, and the gandharvas took perfumes.
In the same list from the Mahabharata, the snakes milked poison, the asuras milked wine, and the yakshas milked the power of invisibility, each with their own calf and vessel.
The Matsya Purana lists who milked the earth: the rakshasas took blood, the nagas poison, and the mountains used a crystal vessel with the Himalaya as calf.
The Mahabharata explains his titles: he is Prithu because he became famous, Kshatriya because he saved people from wounds, and Raja because his delighted subjects loved him.
The Atharvaveda credits Prithu with inventing the plough and flattening rocky land so that farming and cattle-raising could begin.
The Mahabharata describes a golden age in his time: crops grew without ploughing, cows gave milk at a touch, lotuses were full of honey and kusa grass was golden.
In the same account the ocean's waves became firm when he crossed, mountains opened a path for him and his chariot flag was never blocked.
At his horse sacrifice, the Mahabharata says Prithu gave Brahmins gold images of everything on earth and 66,000 golden elephants.
The Bhagavata Purana says he performed ninety-nine horse sacrifices before Indra interrupted the hundredth. He later forgave Indra, and Vishnu blessed him.
The Bhagavata Purana says Archi came out together with Prithu and became his queen. She is regarded as an avatar of Lakshmi, the wife of Vishnu.
A Rig Veda hymn describes Prithu as a rishi, a seer. One scholar suggests the Vedic Prithu was a vegetarian deity linked with Soma, and compared with the Greek god Dionysus.

Prithudaka means 'Prithu's pool'. This town on the Sarasvati's bank is linked with Prithu performing his father's rites, is called the boundary of northern and central India, and is mentioned by Patanjali.
The Bhagavata Purana says the four Kumaras, sage forms of Vishnu, taught Prithu about devotion. After ruling a long time he left for the forest with Archi to do penance.

quiz.q: In the story, what form did the Earth take when she ran away from Prithu?
quiz.why: The Earth fled as a cow and then agreed to be milked.

quiz.q: Who was the calf when Prithu milked the Earth for humans?
quiz.why: Swayambhuva Manu is named as the calf in the Puranas.

quiz.q: What was the name of Prithu's celestial bow in the Vishnu Purana?
quiz.why: The heavens gave him the bow Ajagava along with arrows.

quiz.q: Whom do Hindus regard Prithu as an avatar of?
quiz.why: Hindu tradition regards him as an avatar of Vishnu.

quiz.q: According to the Atharvaveda, what did Prithu invent?
quiz.why: The Atharvaveda credits him with the plough and with levelling land for farming.
